claims.text: The target material is a refractory high-entropy alloy based on W, Ta, Mo, Nb, and V with Group IV hydride precursors such as TiH2 or ZrH2.
The initial powder must have an oxygen content below 50 ppm.
Hydride decomposition should be conducted at 400–600°C.
Ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Torr or an inert argon atmosphere permits hydrogen removal without oxidation of the Group IV elements.
The temperature ramp rate during hydride decomposition should remain below 10°C/min.
Sintering and extrusion should be performed rapidly at 1200–1400°C under oxygen-free conditions.
An extrusion strain rate of approximately 10^-2 s^-1 is required.
The oxygen partial pressure must remain below 10^-15 atm to prevent oxygen uptake.
The proposed high-temperature extrusion and sintering step produces densification while suppressing nucleation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
Post-extrusion cooling faster than 100°C/s kinetically traps a metastable BCC solid solution.
The retained high-temperature BCC phase is ductile.
Alpha-HCP precipitation is thermodynamically favored relative to the metastable BCC phase.
Oxygen exclusion suppresses oxide formation on the Group IV elements.
Oxygen exposure and thermal gradients trigger alpha-HCP precipitation and catastrophic cracking.
Avoiding brittle alpha-HCP precipitation lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
The process will produce a dense bulk alloy with less than 1% porosity.
The processed alloy will exhibit no catastrophic cracking.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000°C.
The processed alloy will have a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature below room temperature.
Conventional powder-metallurgy routes involving air exposure or slow cooling cause alpha-HCP precipitation, oxygen embrittlement, and catastrophic cracking during extrusion.

contradictions.description: The proposed mechanism predicts that oxygen exposure above the specified 10^-15 atm limit should increase alpha-HCP formation and embrittlement. Therefore, observing alpha-HCP above 5% or fracture toughness below 20 MPa·m^1/2 after intentional exposure at 10^-10 atm would support the proposed oxygen-mediated mechanism rather than falsify it.
